items.title: SAML SSO and SOC 2 Type II
items.problem: Enterprise buyers will not add a vendor that sits outside their identity provider or lacks a SOC 2 Type II report; Vantage's 300k expansion is gated on both, and three more security-led prospects stalled on the same ask.

evidence.quote: no SAML SSO and no SOC 2 Type II report, no expansion
We need SAML single sign-on through Okta, with SCIM provisioning if possible.
No SSO and SOC 2 Type II is still pending. This blocks our expansion.
SSO/SAML took an extra round of back-and-forth with your team to configure correctly
Our IT team needs SAML SSO via Okta before more attorneys can be added.
SAML SSO. Our clients' security teams will not allow another password. SOC 2 report as well.
SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, and a VPC deployment in our own cloud account.
We need SOC 2 Type II and ideally a private VPC deployment
Our customers ask for SSO and SOC 2 evidence from sub-processors.
SSO required by their own customers' security review.
Deliver SAML SSO and a SOC 2 Type II report to Vantage.

suggested.rationale: Largest single ARR at stake (480k plus 300k expansion) and recurs in 6 accounts. SAML+SCIM is well-understood; Type II audit window is calendar-bound, not engineering-bound.

items.title: P1 support response SLA and priority queue
items.problem: A nine-hour first reply during an outage cost Clearline trust; several accounts now ask for a written response-time commitment and free-tier delays make evaluators doubt paid support.

evidence.quote: We need a written SLA. One hour response on P1, in the contract.
P1 ticket opened at 02:10, no reply until 11:30. We need a real support response time guarantee.
They want a written support SLA with a 1 hour response on P1 tickets.
Guaranteed support response time during events.
Friday night on-sale broke and the ticket sat in the queue for hours. Need a response SLA for events.
We need a support SLA, an hour for P1.
A support response time commitment would calm our operations team.
support took over 24 hours to raise it
Support replied after four days.
support response has been slow
Contractual 1-hour P1 support response SLA.

suggested.rationale: Mostly process and tooling (P1 queue, paging rota) rather than product code; high confidence it fixes the stated complaint.

items.title: Android SDK streaming parity with iOS
items.problem: The Android SDK has no streaming playback, so Android-heavy customers pre-render audio or delay features; Junction renewed on a promise of parity.

evidence.quote: The Android SDK, though, is noticeably behind
Android SDK with streaming playback parity with iOS.
The Android SDK still has no streaming playback. iOS has had it for most of a year.
Android SDK crashes when streaming is attempted.
Streaming audio does not work on Android. We pre-render everything, which is slow.
Half of our drivers are on Android and your Android SDK cannot stream.
Half their users are on Android.
Android streaming for offline-first guides?
Ship Android SDK with streaming playback parity with iOS.

suggested.rationale: Five accounts plus a renewal commitment; iOS implementation is a reference so scope is known.

items.title: Natural Modern Standard and Gulf-dialect Arabic voices
items.problem: Existing Arabic voices sound robotic and diacritics are handled inconsistently; Beacon's three-year deal is conditional on both MSA and Gulf-dialect voices.

evidence.quote: Gulf dialect voice is the deciding factor for the three-year deal
Gulf dialect for features, and clean Modern Standard Arabic for news bulletins.
Arabic voices sound robotic. We need a natural Gulf dialect.
diacritics handling is inconsistent
Arabic could be a second wish.
then Arabic for Gulf plants
Deliver Modern Standard and Gulf-dialect Arabic voices.

suggested.rationale: One large account plus two weaker signals; dialect data collection and diacritic handling are the unknowns, hence 14 pw.

items.title: VPC / private-cloud deployment
items.problem: Healthcare, banking and public-sector buyers cannot send audio through a shared multi-tenant endpoint; Solace's renewal is gated on a HIPAA-ready VPC deployment by mid-March.

evidence.quote: We need a VPC deployment in our own cloud account, with keys we control.
Legal wants a VPC deployment with a BAA.
Is a VPC or private cloud deployment available?
Only if it is in our cloud account. HIPAA review is strict.
We would pay a premium for private cloud.
Some carriers want it on-prem or in a private cloud.
An on-prem or private cloud installation is the only way we could use you.
They also asked whether an on-prem or private cloud install is possible because of data residency rules.
a Germany-resident deployment option
Could we run it on-prem inside the studio?
Offer VPC deployment with BAA for HIPAA workloads.

suggested.rationale: Seven accounts and 360k committed, but this is new architecture; low confidence on effort, so it is oversized and spans two months.

items.title: Reliable webhooks: retries, signing, delivery log
items.problem: Failed webhooks are dropped silently with no retry or log, so customers find out from their own users; Rapidfire's renewal carries a credit if guarantees are not live by end of March.

evidence.quote: We need retries with backoff, signed payloads, and a log we can search.
Need retries with backoff, signing secrets and a delivery log.
A retry-with-backoff on your end would fix this for us.
Webhook for job completion did not fire for 3 jobs. No retry, no log.
Webhooks silently dropped again.
Webhook signing secrets and retries with backoff are must-haves for dispatch.
They fail without a retry. We need retries and a delivery log or we will poll instead.
We found out from our customers, not from you.
Webhook failures are also invisible.
our order-ready webhooks sometimes vanish.
Webhook delivery guarantees: retries, signing, delivery log.

suggested.rationale: Six accounts independently describe the same fix; standard queue-with-backoff pattern.

items.title: Sub-300 ms time-to-first-byte streaming tier
items.problem: Real-time voice agents, live dubbing and phone ordering need first audio under 300 ms; measured 600-1200 ms today. Chatterbox already delayed its launch waiting for a promised low-latency tier.

evidence.quote: our use case needs sub-300ms to feel conversational.
We delayed our public launch by a month specifically to wait for a lower-latency streaming tier we were told was coming.
Ship the low-latency streaming tier and a volume pricing plan
Latency over 300 milliseconds feels like a dropped call to customers.
we need to go below three hundred milliseconds.
We measure latency at 600 milliseconds.
That is too slow. Passengers are already walking away by the time the voice starts.
Then we can't go live.
latency is far too high for live use
Time to first byte is the whole product for us.
Latency spiked to nearly a second during the evening peak on the EU endpoint.
Latency is hurting phone orders.
Benchmark shows time to first byte of about 650 ms in Seoul.
Says anything over 300 ms to first audio breaks conversation flow.
Latency has to come down for phone ordering.

suggested.rationale: Widest demand in the data (12+ accounts across every source) and the most-cited blocker for real-time use cases. Needs infra plus regional endpoints, so oversized.

items.title: Hindi voices
items.problem: No Hindi voice blocks India-based accounts, a school pilot and an IVR replacement.

evidence.quote: Translation agency needs Hindi urgently, 40 percent of their pipeline.
Schools in India want Hindi narration.
Wants Hindi and a pay-as-you-go option
No Hindi voices yet which is a problem for our largest region.
Hindi voices would unlock the school pilot.
Hindi first. Our largest user base is in India
Hindi voice is a must for our IVR
Japanese and Hindi first
Also still waiting on Hindi.

suggested.rationale: Eight accounts, mostly small-to-mid ARR; shares data and tooling with the Arabic work.

items.title: Usage analytics dashboard and API
items.problem: Customers cannot see minutes used per project, campaign, property or program, so finance rebuilds reports by hand; the existing usage view also lags billing by a day.

evidence.quote: Wants a usage dashboard with per-project breakdown and CSV export.
Per-project breakdown, CSV export, and a monthly email.
Finance keeps asking how many minutes each project used.
usage analytics with per-project breakdown and CSV export
they would pay more for a usage report API
Want a usage API to pull minutes and cost into our BI tool.
Agency bills clients by campaign and has no per-campaign usage report.
Usage analytics by campaign would make billing clients simpler.
A usage dashboard. I cannot tell which show uses how many minutes.
An analytics dashboard to see minutes used by program.
The usage dashboard lags behind actual billing by about a day
They also need to split usage by property for cost allocation.
Need a usage report split by property for cost allocation.

suggested.rationale: Ten accounts including Northwind (275k), who tie expansion to it; metering data already exists for billing. Also unblocks usage-based pricing.

items.title: Usage-based (pay-as-you-go) pricing tier
items.problem: The flat seat plan is wrong for spiky or small workloads; prospects want per-minute billing with overage caps and cost that scales with usage.

evidence.quote: pay-as-you-go per-minute pricing would let them start immediately
A per-minute pay-as-you-go tier plus a usage dashboard would close this next week.
usage-based billing with overage caps is a must
pay-as-you-go option so cost scales with active students
Also prefers pay-as-you-go.
want usage-based pricing
pay-as-you-go would suit
Pay-as-you-go per minute. We have huge peaks around events and nothing in between.
A per-minute pay-as-you-go plan is the only way our model works.
Usage-based, per-minute. Order volume swings with festivals.
Pay-as-you-go would let us start small.
Usage-based pricing would be fairer to our smaller shows.
Flat plan is wasteful for a small show. Want pay-as-you-go per-minute pricing.
Want per-minute billing with overage caps.

suggested.rationale: Fourteen records across sales, support and VoC; mostly SMB/mid ARR but several are ready to close. Needs metering visibility first.

items.title: Pronunciation dictionary / shared lexicon
items.problem: Names, acronyms and terminology are mispronounced and the fix does not persist, so teams re-record or maintain manual overrides.

evidence.quote: We've had to add a pronunciation dictionary manually, which took a couple hours to get right.
A pronunciation dictionary is the first thing I would ask for.
A shared pronunciation lexicon would be huge.
a few of our stations get mispronounced and we've had to add manual overrides.
Pronunciation keeps drifting between generations.
We spend hours re-recording because author names are mispronounced.
Pronunciation of author surnames is hit and miss.
Pronunciation dictionary for product names across all voices, please.
Also wants a custom pronunciation lexicon so product names are read correctly every time.
Narrative designers fight the engine every time a character name is mispronounced.
A shared lexicon across the whole catalog would save them hours each week.
Also need to correct pronunciation once and have it stick across books.
Add words once, and every voice respects them.
Librarians read author names all day and the tool keeps getting them wrong.

suggested.rationale: Ten accounts, every source type; a lexicon layer is a well-bounded feature with a clear success test.

items.title: Recorded voice-clone consent workflow
items.problem: Clone creation already verifies consent at a single point, but agencies, studios and narrators need an auditable per-voice consent record they can show their clients and talent.

evidence.quote: Their compliance team also wants documented consent from any person whose voice is cloned, before the clone can be used.
an explicit consent record for each cloned voice would help legally.
Narrator contracts now require signed consent before a voice clone is created.
Brands also ask for proof that talent consented to voice cloning.
Client asked for proof the voice talent consented to being cloned.
A consent workflow that records permission would help.
Narrators now want signed voice clone consent.
Narrators want written consent before any voice clone is created.
A consent workflow that records permission would protect us legally.

suggested.rationale: Six accounts; legal exposure rather than revenue blocker today but a growing contractual requirement.

items.title: Unity and Unreal engine plugins
items.problem: Game studios hand-wrap the REST API in-engine every sprint; some will not adopt without a plugin.

evidence.quote: Engineers would love a native Unity plugin so they stop wrapping the REST API.
Studio wants an Unreal and Unity plugin.
Unreal Engine plugin.
A proper Unity plugin would save us a sprint each release.
Is there a Unity plugin? We are hand-wrapping the HTTP calls and it is tedious.
Looking for an Unreal Engine plugin.
A native Unity plugin would cut that, and an Unreal one is next on our list.

suggested.rationale: Five studios (≈250k ARR combined); Unity first, Unreal second, wrapping existing REST client.

items.title: Volume discounts and annual-prepay option
items.problem: Finance teams at scaling accounts want volume tiers or an annual discount; this partly conflicts with the push for pure pay-as-you-go.

evidence.quote: Volume discounts past a certain threshold, or a flat monthly tier for high-usage studios
rough pricing pain as we scale
The lack of an annual prepay discount option made it hard to justify to finance
The character pricing didn't help
we're watching the pricing closely as our user base grows

suggested.rationale: Five VoC mentions but no sales-led deal; confidence low because it pulls against the usage-based request.

items.title: Streaming/websocket docs, SDK examples and SSO setup guide
items.problem: Docs for websocket streaming, SDK examples and SSO configuration trail the REST docs.

evidence.quote: the websocket streaming docs are thinner than the REST docs
An end-to-end tutorial for a real-time conversational agent
The Python SDK examples are a bit behind
the self-serve docs for SSO setup are thinner than the rest of the docs

suggested.rationale: Three accounts; low risk, cheap, but low commercial impact.

items.title: Clean interruption (barge-in) handling for voice agents
items.problem: When a caller talks over the agent, audio keeps playing for almost a second.

evidence.quote: Interruption handling is rough
there's an awkward overlap for almost a second

suggested.rationale: Single account, but it affects every IVR/agent use case; needs latency work first to measure.

items.title: Consistent reading of times, numbers and dates

evidence.quote: sometimes comes out with an odd pause
we manually spot-check every announcement with a time or date in it before publishing

suggested.rationale: One SMB account.

evidence.quote: we need Swedish and Finnish for Nordic clients
pitch accent still sounds slightly off on certain words

items.title: Swahili voices

evidence.quote: Swahili voices; maybe Arabic later.
Swahili would be great.

items.title: Multi-speaker dialogue in one generation call
items.problem: Teams generate each character separately and stitch audio by hand.

evidence.quote: Multi-speaker dialogue in a single generation call would save us so much post-production work.

suggested.rationale: One account claiming half of editing time saved.

items.title: Inline emotion tags in the API
items.problem: Studios maintain a dozen presets per character instead of tagging emotion inline.

evidence.quote: Emotion tags in the API
as our character roster grows it's becoming a real maintenance burden.

suggested.rationale: One account; self-described nice-to-have.

items.title: Bulk-job status and per-item failure reporting
items.problem: Batch jobs do not say which files or chapters failed, so teams check outputs manually.

evidence.quote: when we submit 50 files at once, we can't easily see which ones failed
If one chapter fails mid-batch, the whole batch doesn't tell you which chapter failed in the response

suggested.rationale: Two accounts describe the same gap; small API and dashboard change.

items.title: Predictable rate-limit windows and self-serve raises
items.problem: Limits reset unpredictably at midnight UTC and a limit hit during a deadline took more than a day to raise.

evidence.quote: The rate limits reset unpredictably around midnight UTC rather than a clear rolling window
We hit our rate limit during a compliance deadline crunch

suggested.rationale: Two accounts; one near-churn incident already handled manually.

items.title: Multiple billing contacts per account
items.problem: Only one contact receives invoice emails; a missed payment triggered a service-pause warning.

evidence.quote: our account has two different billing contacts and only one of them receives the invoice emails

suggested.rationale: One account; trivial fix, avoids a payment-failure incident.

items.title: Dashboard transcript search and dark mode

evidence.quote: Search within our generated audio library is basically just filename matching
Nice to have: dark mode in the dashboard.
Also asked for dark mode, nice to have.

evidence.quote: Can you build a Salesforce connector? Not urgent.
Also asked for a Salesforce connector, but that is not a priority.

items.title: Automated migration of voice presets
